messages.subject: PopGen workshop - follow-up question
parts:
Hi everyone,
the workshop was great and I am still processing all the information I was supposed to absorb, so I feel I will have more questions as I go through all the material.

However, there are a couple of probably naive questions that I haven't got the chance to ask, so I am hoping I can get some feedback or discussions started about them now here.

Specifically, I would like to know: 

1) Sampling design for fine-scale structure detection
if there are any guidelines for sampling design in terms of number of individuals per location and distance in between sampling locations.
I am aware that this depends on the specific question to address, but when you are conducting a population structure study and want to also detect fine-scale genetic structure (i.e. sampling locations pairwise distances ~ 200 km each), would 20 individuals per location be enough? I find that sometimes, even with 20 individuals per sampling location, you don't have enough power to tell whether the very small significant Fst between locations are biologically relevant. Would 40 individuals per location allow you to be more confident that the very low Fsts represent actually low structure and you are not missing out on greater structure? As your population/sampling group size  also affects the MAF filtering you can apply, I would just like to have some guidance on this.
I am not sure if I explained the problem clearly.

2) Hierarchical Fsts vs AMOVA?
I would like to know if anyone uses Hierarchical Fsts as I just recently tried to use them, by manually pooling nearby locations/pops with not-significant Fst, but by pooling one or the other location first, you can get different downstream results and I feel this process can be quite biased. At the workshop, I was recommended to use "Spatial Autocorrelation" instead of hierarchical Fsts to look at local patterns of structure, but then my question is "are we still using hierarchical Fsts"? And when? Also, when is it better to use them vs. AMOVA instead?

I would appreciate any feedback or discussion on these topics! 
Thanks a lot everyone for an amazing workshop!
Best,
Gabriella
